issues.detail: Error handling is limited to displaying error.message on write; it does not cover wallet rejection, connector failures, missing wallet extensions, or the wrong-network flow with working code.

The two examples are prose summaries with only inline snippets (the balance example uses a vague 'formatted-style' phrasing and the upgrade example has no before/after code), so they are less concrete than runnable demonstrations.

scenarios.name: nextjs-wallet-connect-setup
scenarios.rationale: A follows the rubric closely (wagmi 3 hooks useConnection/useConnect mutate/useConnectors, config with ssr and cookieStorage, providers with useState QueryClient, and the @walletconnect/ethereum-provider install), whereas B uses wagmi v2 style hooks (useAccount, connect from useConnect, no useConnectors or useConnection) so it misses the wagmi 3 requirement despite a solid config and providers.

scenarios.name: send-usdc-with-status-and-decimals
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric most closely: it uses the mutate form of useWriteContract, passes chainId 8453 to transfer, parses with parseUnits at 6 decimals, and mentions useSimulateContract and useSwitchChain, while A uses writeContractAsync instead of the required mutate form and has no explicit 8453 constant, although it does use base.id and handles network switching with useSwitchChain.

scenarios.name: upgrade-wagmi-v2-to-v3
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric item: the install command with wagmi@3, viem@2, react-query@5 and TS ^5.9.3, the useConnection and useConnectors renames, `mutate: writeContract`, connector SDKs, and `npx tsc --noEmit`. A gets the two renames right but says no writeContract change is needed, which is wrong, and it uses loose versions with TS 5.7+ instead of 5.9.3.
